title: Drive unit internal fault
shortDescription: General internal fault in the Yamaha PW drive unit.
fullDescription:
YA-10 is a generic internal drive-unit error. Usually it can be cleared by a system reboot; persistent faults require dealer diagnostics.

Remove the battery for 30 seconds, reinstall and power on.

fixSteps.title: Dealer diagnostic
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, visit Yamaha dealer.

whenToCallPro: If reboot does not fix it.

title: Torque sensor error
fullDescription: YA-20 usually appears when the bike was turned on with feet on the pedals. Restart without load to clear it.

fixSteps.title: Restart unloaded
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove feet from pedals, power on.

whenToCallPro: If error persists despite correct startup.

faq.a: Torque sensor needs a zero reading at boot.

title: Speed sensor error
shortDescription: Speed sensor signal lost or invalid.
fullDescription: YA-30 indicates the speed sensor is not being read correctly. Inspect the spoke magnet and sensor gap.

fixSteps.title: Check magnet
fixSteps.instruction: Align magnet within 5-8 mm of sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install Yamaha OEM sensor if damaged.

faq.q: How tight should the magnet be?
faq.a: Firm enough not to move, not bent on the spoke.

title: Battery communication error
fullDescription: YA-40 means the drive unit cannot talk to the battery. Clean contacts and reseat the battery.

fixSteps.title: Clean and reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Clean battery and frame contacts; refit battery.

fixSteps.title: Dealer test
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, battery test at dealer.

faq.q: Is it always a battery issue?

title: Battery temperature out of range
shortDescription: Battery too hot or cold to operate.
fullDescription: YA-50 appears when battery temperature is outside the operating range. Warm or cool the battery to room temperature before use.
whenToCallPro: If fault appears at moderate temperature.

title: Motor overheat
fullDescription:
YA-60 triggers when the motor reaches its thermal limit. Assist is cut until temperature drops.

Rest for 10-20 minutes and continue at lower assist.
whenToCallPro: If it appears under light load.

faq.a: Assist is cut to prevent damage.

title: Display communication error
shortDescription: Display to drive unit link lost.
fullDescription: YA-70 means the display cable or connector has a fault. Inspect handlebar and motor-end connectors.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and replug both ends of the display cable.

faq.a: Yes, water in the connector is common.

title: Firmware mismatch
fullDescription: YA-80 means the firmware versions of the motor, battery, or display are not compatible. Update at a Yamaha dealer.

fixSteps.title: Dealer firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Have all components updated to latest compatible firmware.

title: Charger error
fullDescription: YA-90 is reported when the battery cannot complete a charge cycle. Use only Yamaha chargers and inspect for damage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect charger
fixSteps.instruction: Check LEDs and cable for damage.

whenToCallPro: If a known good charger still errors.

faq.a: No, risk of damage and fire.

title: Severe drive unit fault
fullDescription: YA-100 is a critical motor fault. Assist is disabled and the unit requires dealer inspection or replacement.

faq.a: Usually yes if in the warranty period.
